item.title: Ise Jingu Kagura: Sacred Music and Dance at Ise — Guide
item.description: Beyond the quiet act of prayer, Ise Jingu preserves kagura — formal ceremonies of sacred music and dance offered to the deities on a worshipper’s behalf. Performed in the kaguraden halls of both the Naiku and Geku by shrine musicians in courtly costume and miko shrine maidens, these rituals set ancient gagaku court music and slow, stylised dance to convey prayers for health, gratitude or family blessing. Anyone can request a kagura offering for a fee, making it a rare opportunity to witness — and personally commission — living ceremonial tradition at the heart of Japan’s most sacred shrine.
